newsitem.title: UK: Shell's second quarter earnings hit by pound.
newsitem.headline: Shell's second quarter earnings hit by pound.

text.p: Oil giant Royal Dutch/Shell Group Thursday reported a four percent fall in second-quarter profit, hit by the strength of the pound, which masked an underlying three percent rise over last year.
Net earnings excluding special items were 1.14 billion pounds ($1.8 billion) in the quarter, making 2.69 billion pounds ($4.3 billion) for the first six months.
Shell said higher production largely offset lower crude oil prices, while chemical earnings were slightly down in the quarter.
Shell shares fell in London and Amsterdam after the results, which came in below market forecasts of between 1.26 billion ($2.0 billion) and 1.48 billion pounds ($2.4 billion).
Shell said refining and marketing margins were up 17 percent in the quarter on a current cost basis, but reported earnings were lower because of inventory holding losses.
Corporate items in the period included currency exchange losses of 117 million pounds ($188 million) due largely to the strength of sterling over the quarter.
The group spent 1.7 billion pounds ($2.7 billion) on capital investment and exploration in the quarter and said spending was set to step up in the second half, mainly on exploration and production.
Shell shares, which have had a strong run recently, were down 30 pence to 443 after the results, while in Amsterdam, shares in the Dutch arm, Royal Dutch, fell 4.70 guilders to 115.50.
